questions.enonce_markdown:
Define the following terms used in digestion.

(i) Absorption

(ii) Enzymes

(iii) Metabolism

(2 marks) + (2 marks) + (2 marks) = (6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Absorption (2 marks).** The passage of the **soluble end products of digestion** (glucose, amino acids, fatty acids and glycerol, vitamins, mineral salts and water) **from the alimentary canal into the blood or lymph**, mainly through the villi of the small intestine.

**(ii) Enzymes (2 marks).** **Biological catalysts**: protein substances made by living cells that **speed up chemical reactions without being used up** themselves. In digestion, they break large insoluble food molecules into small soluble ones.

**(iii) Metabolism (2 marks).** The **sum of all the chemical reactions that take place in the cells of the body**: the breaking down of nutrients to release energy and the building up of new body materials from them.
themes: digestion of food in the human body
energy from food and body metabolism

questions.enonce_markdown:
State and explain three (3) uses of energy in the body.

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The body gets its energy from the food it eats (carbohydrates, fats and proteins). Three uses of this energy are the following.

1. **Keeping the body warm (2 marks).** Energy released in the cells is changed to heat, which keeps the body temperature steady and the body working properly, even in cold surroundings.

2. **Muscular activity and movement (2 marks).** Energy is needed for walking, working, playing and every other movement. The more active a person is, the more energy he or she needs.

3. **Working of the internal organs (2 marks).** Even at rest, energy is used for the heartbeat, breathing, digestion and the work of the brain and nerves. This is called the basal metabolism.
themes: energy from food and body metabolism

questions.corrige_markdown:
1. **Mouth** (where food is chewed and mixed with saliva).
2. **Stomach** (where food is churned and protein digestion begins).
3. **Small intestine** (where digestion is completed and the digested food is absorbed).

(The oesophagus, the large intestine, the liver and the pancreas are also acceptable.)
themes: digestion of food in the human body

questions.enonce_markdown:
Identify five (5) digestive enzymes and the nutrient they act on.

(10 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
| Digestive enzyme | Where it is found | Nutrient it acts on | Product |
|---|---|---|---|
| Salivary amylase | Mouth (saliva) | Starch (carbohydrate) | Maltose |
| Pepsin | Stomach (gastric juice) | Proteins | Peptides |
| Trypsin | Small intestine (from the pancreas) | Proteins | Peptides and amino acids |
| Lipase | Small intestine (from the pancreas) | Fats and oils | Fatty acids and glycerol |
| Maltase | Small intestine (intestinal juice) | Maltose (sugar) | Glucose |

Each enzyme with the correct nutrient earns 2 marks (5 x 2 = 10 marks).
themes: digestion of food in the human body
